body.text: Which surgeries (eyelid, minor lipo, rhinoplasty) can be done solo with a hotel nurse vs which require a companion?

Procedures with limited mobility impact—such as upper blepharoplasty, small-area liposuction, or uncomplicated rhinoplasty—can often be managed solo if you book hospital observation plus scheduled private hotel nurse visits. Extensive surgeries like tummy tucks, mommy makeovers, facelifts, or large-volume liposuction require 24-hour hands-on assistance, either from a companion or hired private nursing.

Always align your solo recovery plan with international safety standards such as the [ISAPS Safety Considerations](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/safety-considerations/) and [NHS Cosmetic Surgery Abroad advice](https://www.nhs.uk/tests-and-treatments/cosmetic-procedures/advice/cosmetic-surgery-abroad/). Confirm that your hospital holds a valid [Turkish Ministry of Health International Health Tourism Authorization Certificate](https://shgmturizmdb.saglik.gov.tr/EN-69289/healthcare-providers-with-international-health-tourism-authorization-certificates.html) before paying any deposit.

body.text: How many nights of hospital + private nursing care keep solo patients safe?

For general-anaesthetic procedures, solo patients should budget at least 1 to 2 inpatient hospital nights followed by 2 to 5 days of private hotel nursing, depending on surgical extent. Never discharge straight to an empty hotel room on the evening of general anaesthesia without supervised overnight monitoring.

Flight timing matters just as much as hospital nights. According to [BAPRAS Cosmetic Surgery Abroad guidance](https://www.bapras.org.uk/public/patient-information/cosmetic-surgery/cosmetic-surgery-abroad), patients should generally wait 5 to 7 days before flying after breast surgery or liposuction, and 7 to 10 days after facial procedures. Your operating surgeon determines your exact fit-to-fly clearance and inpatient stay, and [ISAPS guidance on planning procedures abroad](https://www.isaps.org/discover/patients-home/considering-your-procedure-abroad/make-a-plan/) stresses building buffer days into your itinerary for follow-up checks.
What tasks (medications, dressing, airport luggage) cannot be done alone post-op?

After general anaesthesia, pain medication, swelling, and surgical drains make routine tasks surprisingly difficult. Solo patients routinely underestimate how hard it is to track timed antibiotics and blood thinners, fasten compression garments, change sterile dressings, rise safely from low hotel beds, or handle suitcases at the airport.

items: Medication tracking: General anaesthesia and analgesics cause grogginess, making missed or doubled doses a real risk without a written schedule or nurse check.
Compression garments and drains: Fastening tight post-op corsets, emptying surgical drains, and checking incision sites behind your line of sight require a second pair of hands.
Basic mobility and hygiene: Standing up after abdominal or body-contouring surgery, washing hair without wetting incisions, and picking up dropped items can strain sutures.
Airport luggage and transfers: Lifting bags onto scales or into overhead bins is unsafe post-op; pre-book wheelchair assistance and airport porter service.

faq.q: Can hotel staff help me change dressings or take medication?
faq.a: No. Hotel staff are hospitality workers, not licensed clinicians. They can deliver ice, extra pillows, or room service, but medical tasks require a licensed nurse or your surgical team.

faq.q: Is hiring a private recovery nurse cheaper than flying a companion?
faq.a: Often yes, especially for 2 to 4 days of scheduled visits, and a licensed nurse brings clinical observation skills that a well-meaning friend or family member does not have.

faq.q: How early should I book airport wheelchair assistance?
faq.a: Request special assistance through your airline at least 48 to 72 hours before departure so staff are ready at check-in, security, and boarding gates in Istanbul or Antalya.

faq.q: Can I stay in an Airbnb instead of a hotel after solo plastic surgery?
faq.a: A full-service hotel with a 24-hour reception, elevator, and room service is usually safer solo than a private apartment with stairs, lockboxes, and no on-site staff.

faq.q: What if my surgeon recommends extending my stay before flying home?
faq.a: Always book flexible or changeable return tickets and leave budget for extra hotel nights. Never fly against medical advice to save a ticket change fee.
